description: Add complete AI company role-based agent presets and a CompanyOrchestrator that can break down complex tasks, assign sub-tasks to specialized agents, pipe outputs between agents, run independent sub-tasks simultaneously, and collect results. Also add enhanced fleet API endpoints for remote orchestration with task-ID tracking.
steps:
Step 1 - Create new company role preset modules in agentwork/presets/company/. Follow the same pattern as agentwork/presets/office.py (decorated tool functions + factory function returning Agent). Create these files:
  - agentwork/presets/company/__init__.py (exports all company presets)
  - agentwork/presets/company/ceo.py - CEOAgent with tools: strategic_planning, decision_maker, task_delegator
  - agentwork/presets/company/cto.py - CTOAgent with tools: architecture_designer, tech_stack_evaluator, code_reviewer
  - agentwork/presets/company/developer.py - DeveloperAgent with tools: code_generator, bug_fixer, test_writer, code_refactorer
  - agentwork/presets/company/designer.py - DesignerAgent with tools: ui_designer, mockup_creator, brand_styler
  - agentwork/presets/company/content_writer.py - ContentWriterAgent with tools: article_writer, copywriter, technical_writer
  - agentwork/presets/company/hr.py - HRAgent with tools: recruiter, onboarding_manager, performance_reviewer
  - agentwork/presets/company/finance.py - FinanceAgent with tools: budget_planner, invoice_processor, financial_reporter
  - agentwork/presets/company/support.py - CustomerSupportAgent with tools: ticket_handler, faq_responder, escalation_manager
  - agentwork/presets/company/project_manager.py - ProjectManagerAgent with tools: task_tracker, timeline_planner, status_reporter

Step 2 - Create the CompanyOrchestrator class in agentwork/orchestrator.py. This is a higher-level manager that:
  - Accepts a high-level complex task description and a fleet of specialized agents
  - Breaks the task into sub-tasks (using a configurable decompose_fn callback or a built-in simple splitter)
  - Uses a dependency graph (DAG) to determine execution order, leveraging the existing TaskPlan/Step model from agentwork/engine/planner.py
  - Assigns each sub-task to the best agent via the existing TaskRouter
  - Runs independent sub-tasks simultaneously using asyncio.gather or ThreadPoolExecutor (like Pipeline.run_parallel)
  - Pipes output from one agent's completed sub-task as input to the next dependent sub-task (like Pipeline.run sequential, but across agents)
  - Collects all results into a final CompanyTaskResult with per-agent outputs
  - Never fails: if one agent fails, tries a fallback agent or returns partial results
  - Tracks everything with task_id so remote clients can poll for status
  The class should have methods:
  - orchestrate(task_description, input_data, task_id=None) -> CompanyTaskResult
  - orchestrate_async(task_description, input_data, task_id=None) -> CompanyTaskResult
  - get_status(task_id) -> dict with per-subtask status
  - add_agent(agent) and remove_agent(agent_name)

Step 3 - Create agentwork/orchestrator.py with a CompanyTaskResult model (extends or wraps TaskResult) that includes:
  - task_id: str
  - status: overall status
  - sub_results: List of {agent_name, sub_task, status, output} dicts
  - final_output: the combined/last output
  - duration_ms: total time
  This is part of step 2 but split for clarity.

Step 4 - Add fleet/orchestrator API endpoints to the server. Create or extend agentwork/server/app.py (or a new file agentwork/server/fleet_app.py) with a create_fleet_app(orchestrator) factory that exposes:
  - POST /fleet/orchestrate - Submit a complex task to the orchestrator (accepts task_id, task_description, input_data). Returns task_id immediately for async tracking.
  - GET /fleet/status/{task_id} - Get orchestration status (which sub-tasks are pending/running/done)
  - GET /fleet/result/{task_id} - Get final result by task_id (only returns to that specific task_id requester)
  - GET /fleet/agents - List all registered agents and their capabilities
  - POST /fleet/agents - Register a new agent dynamically
  - DELETE /fleet/agents/{agent_name} - Remove an agent
  These endpoints use the LRUResultStore pattern from server/app.py for persistence.

Step 5 - Update agentwork/presets/__init__.py to also export the new company presets (CEOAgent, CTOAgent, DeveloperAgent, DesignerAgent, ContentWriterAgent, HRAgent, FinanceAgent, CustomerSupportAgent, ProjectManagerAgent).
Step 6 - Update agentwork/__init__.py to export CompanyOrchestrator and the create_fleet_app function.

Step 7 - Write comprehensive tests:
  - tests/test_company_presets.py: Test all new preset agents can be instantiated, have correct tools, and execute their tools successfully. Follow the pattern in tests/test_presets.py.
  - tests/test_orchestrator.py: Test CompanyOrchestrator can decompose tasks, assign to agents, pipe outputs between sequential agents, run parallel sub-tasks, handle agent failures gracefully (partial results), and track by task_id.
  - tests/test_fleet_api.py: Test the fleet API endpoints using httpx.AsyncClient with the FastAPI TestClient pattern. Test submit orchestration, get status, get result by task_id, list agents.
Step 8 - Ensure all existing tests still pass (python3.12 -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short). Run the full test suite to confirm no regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 new company role preset agents can be instantiated and their tools executed successfully
CompanyOrchestrator can accept a complex task, break it into sub-tasks, and assign them to appropriate agents
Task piping works: output from one agent flows as input to the next dependent agent
Independent sub-tasks run in parallel (simultaneous execution)
If an agent fails, the orchestrator returns partial results rather than crashing
Fleet API endpoints allow remote submission of orchestration tasks with task_id tracking
GET /fleet/result/{task_id} returns results only for that specific task_id
All new tests pass: test_company_presets.py, test_orchestrator.py, test_fleet_api.py
All existing 105 tests continue to pass with no regressions
verification: python3.12 -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short (all tests pass including new ones)
python3.12 -c "from agentwork.presets.company import CEOAgent, CTOAgent, DeveloperAgent, DesignerAgent, ContentWriterAgent, HRAgent, FinanceAgent, CustomerSupportAgent, ProjectManagerAgent"
findings: Implemented parameter-filtering piping logic in the orchestrator to safely pass output from one tool to another even when schemas differ. The orchestrator uses inspect.signature to filter piped kwargs to only include params the target tool accepts, preventing TypeErrors. All 156 tests pass (105 existing + 51 new). The fleet API supports task-ID tracking for remote orchestration with concurrent tasks.
